A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPV framework and JBR pruning method. Their text, equations, figures, references, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v4.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic, CIFAR-10/100, and ImageNet experiments on TPV stability, label-noise sensitivity, and pruning, including supplementary results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical experiments and adds regularization, training-trajectory, and model-selection results, including BERT text-classification and Oxford-IIIT Pets experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3.4 adds adaptive perturbation scaling, sigma = c times sigma_0, where c is the reference model's mean absolute output. This modifies noise generation in the existing perturb-and-retrain estimator. The central trace framework and JBR scoring procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic, CIFAR, and ImageNet coverage, v4 evaluates AG News topic classification and TREC question classification with 20% label corruption, and transfer learning on Oxford-IIIT Pets with 10% corruption. It also adds CIFAR-100 training trajectories under 30% corrupted labels.

E2.justification: The new training-recipe comparison evaluates Jacobian sharpness, Tr(Heff), against training-set label-noise TPV as predictors of test-set sensitivity (Figure 11; Appendix I.4). The pruning comparator set remains Jacobian, L1, BatchNorm scale, FPGM, WHC, Taylor, and Random.

E3.justification: The retained ImageNet experiment's reported protocol changes from 10 SGD epochs at learning rate 10^-6 with fixed sigma = 0.01 to five AdamW epochs at 10^-8 with adaptive noise scaling. New experiments introduce regularization grids, checkpoint-based TPV evaluation, and a two-phase Pets fine-tuning protocol. These are substantive experimental-design changes.

E4.justification: v4 adds single-regularizer sensitivity sweeps examining underfitting and overfitting, plus TPV trajectories through image-classifier training and BERT fine-tuning (Section 5.3; Appendix G.3). These investigate when the TPV–test-loss relationship holds or reverses, beyond v2's retained width, sample-size, and perturbation-size analyses.

E5.justification: v4 newly specifies ImageNet sampling seed 0 and repetition details for added trajectory experiments, including three perturbation runs per BERT checkpoint. Appendix I.4 introduces qualitative Spearman-correlation reporting for recipe rankings. Retained experiments keep their repetition counts; no new confidence-interval or significance-testing framework is introduced.

E6.justification: New results include U-shaped TPV–test-loss relationships for label smoothing and dropout, training-trajectory patterns, Pets model-selection outcomes, and opposing sharpness versus TPV rankings in Figure 11. ImageNet TPV values also change under the revised protocol, rather than demonstrating a same-setting gain. Original pruning and width/stability findings are retained.

T1.justification: The stability theorem now assumes isotropic covariance and replaces the NTK coefficient 2 with (n_train+n_test)/p. Appendix A replaces the spectral-to-operator-norm inference with a trace-based proof. SGD and quantization statements change zero-loss assumptions to small nonzero residuals, and v4 removes the finite-sample assertion X-transpose-X/n = I when n is smaller than the input dimension.

C1.justification: Alongside the retained framework, stability, and pruning contributions, v4 elevates training-set-only model and recipe selection across four deployment scenarios to a main contribution. Its conclusion also adds a two-phase TPV–test-loss relationship, substantially extending and qualifying v2's broad empirical correlation claim.

C2.justification: v4 explains that low TPV can accompany underfitting and higher test loss, restricting useful positive correlation primarily to low-training-loss regimes. It adds weaker cross-architecture reliability and optimizer-dependent applicability limitations in Appendix I. It also explains why sharpness and label-noise sensitivity can respond differently to Jacobian spectral changes.

D1.justification: Appendices D.3.4, G.3, and I provide substantial new reproducibility information: noise calibration, regularization grids, architecture specifications, BERT tokenization, optimizer schedules, checkpoint evaluation, and Pets head replacement and fine-tuning instructions. The code-repository link is unchanged; the addition is primarily technical documentation.

R1.justification: v4 adds connections to information-bottleneck analyses and epoch-wise double descent, citing Tishby and Zaslavsky, Shwartz-Ziv and Tishby, and Nakkiran et al., alongside new dataset and regularization references. Several NTK and spectral-bias references are removed. The central local-versus-global positioning remains, and pruning-related work is retained in Appendix H.2.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, empirical narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work moves earlier, empirical verification and applications become separate sections, and the full JBR derivation and pruning discussion move into a dedicated appendix. This substantially reorganizes the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds regularization, trajectory, and model-selection figures and redraws the ImageNet plot. Original pruning displays are consolidated in Appendix H as Figures 21–24, retaining both MAC and pruned-filter-percentage views. Existing stability figures are also relocated or resized, producing substantial visual reorganization beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important proof gap in v2's Appendix A through an explicit isotropy restriction and trace-based argument. Its new regularization analyses reveal when low TPV indicates underfitting, materially improving interpretation of the proposed generalization signal, while detailed protocols improve reproducibility. The narrower theorem still does not establish every broader model-selection claim, and cross-architecture rankings remain imperfect, but the gains in rigor and applicability boundaries are substantial.
